classification.difficultyReason: Construct a general algebraic divisibility proof using an integer root and integer coefficients.

content.prompt: Suppose that $P(x)=a_nx^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1x+a_0$ is a polynomial with integer coefficients, and suppose that $P(\alpha)=0$, where $\alpha$ is an integer. Show that $\alpha$ is a factor of the constant term $a_0$. This justifies the second dot-point on page 507.

answer.short:
$$a_0=-\alpha\left(a_n\alpha^{n-1}+a_{n-1}\alpha^{n-2}+\cdots+a_1\right).$$
The bracket is an integer, so $\alpha$ divides $a_0$.
answer.worked:
Since $P(\alpha)=0$,
$$a_n\alpha^n+a_{n-1}\alpha^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1\alpha+a_0=0.$$
Rearranging and taking out the common factor $\alpha$ gives
$$\begin{align*}a_0&=-\left(a_n\alpha^n+a_{n-1}\alpha^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1\alpha\right)\\a_0&=-\alpha\left(a_n\alpha^{n-1}+a_{n-1}\alpha^{n-2}+\cdots+a_1\right).\end{align*}$$
Every coefficient and $\alpha$ is an integer, so the bracket is an integer. Thus $a_0$ is an integer multiple of $\alpha$, as required.
